# Routeables

> View-model-first routing for .NET 10. A view model asks an `IRouter` to go to a route; it never touches a page, a frame or a navigation API of the UI framework, so the same view models run on Avalonia, WPF, .NET MAUI, Uno Platform, WinUI 3, Blazor and ASP.NET Core. Routes are found by a source generator at compile time (no reflection: Native AOT and trimming work). MIT license.

What to know before writing code with it:

- Install the package of the host, and only that one: `Routeables.Avalonia`, `Routeables.Wpf`, `Routeables.Maui`, `Routeables.Uno`, `Routeables.WinUI3`, `Routeables.Blazor` or `Routeables.AspNetCore`. It brings `Routeables` (the router and the source generator) and `Routeables.Abstraction`. The .NET 10 SDK is required.
- A page is a view model with `[Routeable("/hello/{name}")]` and a view with the matching name (`HelloViewModel` and `HelloView`). The view derives from `RouteableFor<HelloViewModel>` and receives the view model (`ViewModel`, typed). The values of the address reach the constructor of the view model by name (`HelloViewModel(string name)`).
- A view model navigates with the `IRouter` it asks for in its constructor: `await router.GoToAsync("/hello/Claire");`, `await router.GoBackAsync();`. Never navigate with the API of the UI framework (`Frame.Navigate`, `Shell.GoToAsync`, `NavigationManager.NavigateTo`).
- A region is a zone of the screen that shows pages. On the XAML hosts: `<routeables:RouteableRegion Route="/hello/World" />`, where `Route` is the first page.
- The host is started with `UseRouteables(...)`. The call differs for each host: read the page of the hosts.
- The typed placeholders are `string`, `int`, `long`, `bool`, `guid`, `decimal` and `double` (`{id:int}`). Another type needs a serializer registered by the application.
- The generator and the analyzers report mistakes at compile time with `ROUT` diagnostics (a route that matches no page, several views for one view model, a cached page with parameters). Each one links to its line of the diagnostics page.
- Guards (`IRouteGuard`) allow, refuse or redirect a route change. A view model refuses to be left with `CanLeaveAsync`.

- [Recipes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedric56/Routeables/master/docs/guides/recipes.md): a sign-in guard, master and detail, passing an object, asking before leaving, tabs with their own history

## Guides

- [Routes and templates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedric56/Routeables/master/docs/guides/routes.md): the syntax of a route, placeholders, constraints, the query
- [Typed routing methods](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedric56/Routeables/master/docs/guides/typed-routes.md): the `GoTo...Async` methods the generator writes
- [Passing arguments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedric56/Routeables/master/docs/guides/arguments.md): values, objects and results between pages
- [Lifecycle, guards and events](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedric56/Routeables/master/docs/guides/lifecycle.md): entering, leaving, guards, the events of the router
- [History](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedric56/Routeables/master/docs/guides/history.md): back, forward, limits, saving and restoring
- [Regions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedric56/Routeables/master/docs/guides/regions.md): several zones, tabs, their own history
- [Transitions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedric56/Routeables/master/docs/guides/transitions.md): animations between pages
- [Back, deep links, guards and diagnostics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedric56/Routeables/master/docs/guides/system-integration.md): the back button, deep links, system notifications
- [Hosts, services and samples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedric56/Routeables/master/docs/guides/hosts.md): dialogs, notifications, themes, translating the texts of the library
- [Routeables for Blazor developers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedric56/Routeables/master/docs/guides/blazor.md)
- [Native AOT and trimming](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedric56/Routeables/master/docs/guides/aot.md)
- [Diagnostics reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedric56/Routeables/master/docs/guides/diagnostics.md): every `ROUT` rule, what it means and how to fix it
